_note: English instruction bank for the sim VLA corpus.
This file MUST be committed before any training run. The A3 ablation asks
whether the policy follows *language* or has memorised a handful of strings,
and that question is only answerable if the held-out phrasings were fixed
before the model saw the training set. Adding a phrase to `heldout` after
seeing eval results silently converts the test into a training set.
train    - used to build the training corpus
heldout  - used ONLY for the evaluation corpus, never collected into train
The split is over *surface form*, not over slot values. bay3 must appear in
both splits, otherwise a failure on held-out phrasing is indistinguishable
from a failure on an unseen goal. What differs is how the same request is
Slot policy: every commanded degree of freedom must appear in the sentence.
If speed varies across episodes but is never spoken, the same sentence maps
to several different trajectories and the policy can only learn their mean.
That is why `speed_clause` is appended to every template rather than left

ordinal._note: The car enters the aisle heading +y with all four bays on its right, so bay1 is the one reached first. 'first' is defined by travel order, not by map index.

speed._note: Three levels, mapped to target_speed in the driver. The words must be ordinal-consistent: slow < normal < fast, with no overlap in the numeric values.

lane._note: lane1 is the inner lane (smaller radius), lane2 the outer. Verified against track_paths.json: both sit 1.58 m from the road centreline, 3.16 m apart.

heldout: the lane closer to the centre
the lane closer to the edge

zone._note: Ring waypoints. Names come from zone_map.yaml; the spoken form drops the map's punctuation.

train: Park in the {ordinal} bay on the right, {speed}.
Drive into the {ordinal} parking spot on your right, {speed}.
Park the car in the {ordinal} space, {speed}.
Head into the {ordinal} bay on the right and stop, {speed}.
heldout: Find the {ordinal} bay on your right and park there, {speed}.
I want you in the {ordinal} parking space, {speed}.
Bring the car to a stop inside the {ordinal} bay, {speed}.
Put it in the {ordinal} slot on the right, {speed}.

train: Stay in {lane} and drive up to {zone}, {speed}.
Drive along {lane} and stop when you reach {zone}, {speed}.
heldout: Keep to {lane} and pull up at {zone}, {speed}.

cruise._note: No endpoint in the sentence — the demo's 'start driving' case. Episodes end by duration while still moving; to_lerobot skips hold-frame padding when the terminal speed is not near zero.
train: Just drive around the track in {lane}, {speed}.

speed_map._note: RAW motor units 0..250 — the real car's native speed scale (m/s exists only past the sim Twist boundary: raw/255*5.0, see nav_vla_pkg/speed_control.py). The demonstrator is the tuned YOLO lane-follow stack (user's months of tuning; demonstrations must stay inside its envelope): motion_planner targets raw 150 on straights with a raw 100 corner floor, and /speed_command (Int32, raw) acts as a LIMIT clamp — so tiers are reachable purely via that limit: 70 caps below everything, 110 sits between corner floor and straight target, 150 releases the full tuned speed. Raising past 150 would need target_speed_raw at node startup and leaves tuned territory — only with the user. Corpus v2 used m/s {0.7, 1.2, 1.8} = raw {36, 61, 92} — entirely below the stack's operating band, which is why 'quickly' felt slow.
